_comment: Vendor peak dense FLOP/s PER DEVICE, used only to compute MFU.
IMPORTANT: verify every number against the vendor spec sheet before you
publish anything derived from it, and record where you got it in _source.
On Aurora the device is a TILE (ZE_FLAT_DEVICE_HIERARCHY=FLAT), so these
must be per-tile values -- roughly half the per-GPU figure. Leave a value
as null and MFU is omitted from the results rather than computed wrong.
Do not count sparsity-boosted 2:1 numbers; use dense figures only.

Data Center GPU Max._source: Max 1550 (2-stack): 839 TFLOP/s BF16-FP16 dense, 52 TFLOP/s FP64-FP32 vector, 419 TFLOP/s TF32, per GPU. Halved here for per-tile. CONFIRM on Intel's spec page before publishing -- these came from secondary coverage of Intel's own figures, not the datasheet directly.
Data Center GPU Max._check: Reproduces from the architecture: 128 Xe-cores x 4096 bf16 FLOP/clock x 1.6 GHz = 839 TFLOP/s, and the same method gives 128 x 256 x 1.6 GHz = 52 TFLOP/s FP64, matching Intel's published FP64.
Data Center GPU Max._note: Max 1550 = 2 tiles per GPU; these keys must be per-tile

A100._source: A100 SXM4 40GB (Polaris): 312 TFLOP/s dense BF16/FP16 tensor core. CONFIRM against NVIDIA's A100 datasheet for the SXM4 40GB part before publishing -- and note the widely quoted 624 figure is the 2:1 SPARSE number, which this file's policy excludes.
A100._note: One A100 = one device here, unlike Aurora where the device is a tile. Do not compare these per-device MFU figures without saying so.

cpu._source: UNVERIFIED - Crux AMD EPYC, cores x FMA width x 2 x clock
